prob_closure.status: CLOSED as wired, with new defect N2 and residual N3
prob_closure.evidence: Wiring: internal/domain/client_session_fence.go defines EnsureClientSessionFence over a fenceExec interface, and backupFence calls it with its own *sql.Tx immediately after the Run barrier DDL and before the credential revoke / run loop (git diff --ignore-cr-at-eol 1ae4b831..a34ce37a -- internal/domain/backup_recovery.go returns exactly one added 3-line hunk '@@ -237,6 +237,9 @@ if e = EnsureClientSessionFence(ctx, tx); e != nil { return nil, e }' and nothing else, so no other behaviour in that file changed; the interface is satisfied by *sql.Tx at compile time and I confirmed the call at runtime with my own tx-scoped call). Semantics measured on real migrated databases: epoch regression is blocked with SESSION_EPOCH_REGRESSION even when no barrier row exists (and the trigger is scoped to UPDATE OF writer_epoch, so watermark-only updates are unaffected); with a barrier row and no observation, +1 is refused with RESTORE_FRESH_RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED; an observation with the wrong epoch is refused; an observation older than restored_at is refused; a fresh observation bound to the session's current writer_epoch unlocks exactly one advance and the next advance is refused again; the domain-level HandoffEpoch surfaces the same abort, so the guard is in front of the API W03-02 will call, not just raw SQL. Pre-W03 no-op: against a baseline-only database the helper returns nil and creates nothing (0 objects matching backup_restore_barriers or client_session%), asserted by W0301-FENCE-NOOP-WITHOUT-TABLE and by my own count. Sister-trigger shape: same barrier table, same (project, run) key, same o.epoch = OLD epoch and o.observed_at > restored_at pattern, and observed_at/restored_at both come from domain.Now() (RFC3339Nano) so the string comparison is like-for-like. Two gaps remain: N2 (the unlock is unreachable from production code) and N3 (weaker evidence bar and run_id NULL sessions unfenced).

problems.severity: medium, this card's own file, introduced by the P9 fix
problems.title: MapClientSession stores the three new timestamp fields in Go's time.String() form, not RFC3339/date-time
problems.detail: v24_sessions.go:98-101 formats CreatedAt and UpdatedAt with time.RFC3339Nano but passes LeaseExpiresAt, SealedAt and ArchivedAt to ExecContext as raw *time.Time pointers. The driver dereferences them and the TEXT column receives Go's default String() rendering. Measured on a real migrated database in my own probe: created_at = "2026-10-01T17:49:14.8163139Z" while, in the same row, sealed_at = "2026-10-01 16:49:14.8163247 +0000 UTC" and archived_at = "2026-10-01 17:48:14.8163247 +0000 UTC"; a separate row showed lease_expires_at = "2026-10-01 17:48:45.5168139 +0000 UTC". Consequences I confirmed by execution, not inference: (a) scanning lease_expires_at back into a time.Time fails with 'sql: Scan error on column index 0, name "lease_expires_at": unsupported Scan, storing driver.Value type string into type *time.Time', so the Go layer cannot read what it wrote; (b) the value does not match SQLite's own GLOB '[0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9]-[0-9][0-9]-[0-9][0-9]T*' test, i.e. it is not ISO-8601 and violates the frozen client.protocol.schema.json format 'date-time' required for WriterLease.expires_at and SessionSnapshot.archived_at; (c) one column, sealed_at, ends up holding two different encodings depending on the write path (Seal() writes RFC3339Nano at v24_sessions.go:188, MapClientSession writes String()), so sealed_at is not comparable or orderable as text.
problems.why_the_check_missed_it: tests/domain/check/main.go baseSession() (lines 115-120) never sets LeaseExpiresAt, SealedAt, ArchivedAt, WorkspaceRef or ModelConfigRef - I grepped the file: 'LeaseExpiresAt', 'ArchivedAt' and 'WorkspaceRef' do not appear at all - so every asserted row has those columns NULL and the encoding path is never executed.
problems.fix: format the three pointers with RFC3339Nano when non-nil (same helper as created_at/updated_at) and add one assertion that maps a session with lease_expires_at / sealed_at / archived_at set, reads each back as text, and requires the same shape as created_at plus a successful scan into a time.

problems.severity: medium, this card's own file, introduced by the P10 fix
problems.title: the client-session restore fence can never be satisfied through any production code path
problems.detail: client_session_require_fresh (client_session_fence.go:41-46) blocks an epoch increase unless a runtime_observations row exists with o.epoch = OLD.writer_epoch and o.observed_at later than restored_at. But runtime_observations is keyed by the Run's lease epoch and the only writer in the repository is internal/domain/runtime.go:113 (ObserveRuntime, INSERT ... VALUES(project, runID, epoch, ...)), whose epoch argument is the run's lease_epoch - change_impact.go:108 and runtime.go:121 read it back with r['lease_epoch']. Nothing anywhere writes a row carrying a client session's writer_epoch, and the two counters are not linked (this is exactly the unlink P10 complained about, now reproduced inside the guard). Measured with a run whose body lease_epoch is 7 and a session on that run whose writer_epoch is 3: after EnsureClientSessionFence, a production-shaped fresh observation (epoch 7, children_stopped true, queue_empty true) lets the Run's own lease advance through domain_objects (my D2d, exit clean) while domain.HandoffEpoch on the session is still refused with RESTORE_FRESH_RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED (D2e); inserting a synthetic observation at epoch 3 with body '{}' then lets it through (D2f). Compounding this, the helper seeds a barrier for every open session that has a run_id regardless of that run's status or even whether the run object exists - in one probe the seeded barrier count was 1 for a session whose run had no domain_objects row at all, and sealed or run-less sessions were correctly skipped - so a session attached to a SETTLED run is fenced with evidence that run will never produce again. Net effect: after a single backup restore, writer handoff for the affected sessions is permanently fail-closed and only a raw SQL insert can clear it.
problems.impact: W03-02 implements session.attach/handoff (22 lines 130-147) against this mapping; with the fence as delivered, the documented 'post-restore, reconcile, then re-grant the writer with an incremented epoch' flow (22 line 145) has no reachable success condition.
problems.fix: either bind the session's freshness requirement to the owning Run's lease epoch (write or look up the linkage P10 asked for - e.g. require the observation at the current lease_epoch of domain_objects kind='Run' id = NEW.run_id, and store the run linkage so the two counters are not independent), or scope the seeding to runs that backupFence itself fenced (unfinished statuses) and make the unlock condition satisfiable; in both cases add a check-program assertion that walks the unlock through the production observation shape rather than only asserting the block (today W0301-RESTORED-EPOCH-NEEDS-FRESH-OBSERVATION only proves the refusal).

problems.severity: low, deviation from the sister trigger the checklist asked me to compare
problems.title: session fence demands weaker evidence than the Run fence and leaves run-less sessions uncovered
problems.detail: The Run trigger at backup_recovery.go:236 requires the observation body to carry json_extract(o.body,'$.children_stopped')=1 AND json_extract(o.body,'$.queue_empty')=1. I created both triggers in one database and read their SQL back from sqlite_master: the Run trigger contains both predicates (D3) and client_session_require_fresh contains neither (D4) - my probe unlocked a session epoch advance with body '{}'. So a restored session can be re-handed-off on evidence that would not be accepted for the very Run it points at, which is inconsistent with 22 line 145 ('宿主自身崩溃后先按原 Run/checkpoint/副作用账本对账，再递增 epoch'). Separately the barrier is keyed (project, run), so a session with run_id NULL gets no barrier row at all (measured: 0 barriers for the run-less session, and its epoch advance is only protected against regression, not against re-issuing an epoch a client already holds); the checklist's 'no regression + fresh observation' requirements are met for sessions with a run, and only the regression half applies to session-only work.
problems.fix: mirror the two body predicates (or a documented equivalent reconciliation fact) into client_session_require_fresh, and decide explicitly whether a run-less session needs its own barrier key space; if it does not, say so in the comment instead of leaving the coverage implicit.

problems.severity: low, residual polish from P2 rather than a reopening
problems.title: unknown-id and backwards-watermark identities are still not cleanly separated
problems.detail: domain.AdvanceWatermark and domain.HandoffEpoch on a session id that does not exist return the raw driver error sql.ErrNoRows (measured: 'raw:sql.ErrNoRows'), which a W03-02 handler would have to special-case or it will leak into a client error; domain.Seal on an unknown id returns ErrSealed (sentinel:SESSION_SEALED, v24_sessions.go:174-176), which reads as 'already sealed' for a session that never existed; and a backwards or unchanged watermark is reported as STALE_WRITER_EPOCH (measured on both 4->4 and 4->2) even though the epoch was correct, so a client would be told to refresh its writer lease when the real problem is the sequence. The three sentinels the first round required (STALE_REVISION / SESSION_SEALED / MISSING_WRITER_ATTRIBUTION) are all correct and now asserted, so this is a small remaining mapping-surface issue: one NotFound sentinel plus a dedicated stale-sequence code would finish it.
problems.fix: map sql.ErrNoRows to a single ErrSessionNotFound in all three functions, and return a distinct ErrStaleWatermark when the epoch and revision both matched but the sequence did not move forward.

problems.title: index and registry shapes that do not carry the weight their names suggest
problems.detail: client_sessions_open is CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ... ON client_sessions (project_id, id) WHERE sealed_at IS NULL; since id is already the table's PRIMARY KEY the composite adds no constraint, and I measured that two open sessions in the same project insert cleanly (o1 and o2 under p1, both accepted), so the index does not express 'one open session per project' even though the file header calls this the single-host index. Either make it UNIQUE(project_id) WHERE sealed_at IS NULL or drop it and say in the comment that multi-open is allowed. writer_client_id is NOT NULL but a raw INSERT with '' succeeds (measured: no error), so writer attribution is enforced only in Go - the P9 goal of making the writer attributable would be firmer with CHECK (length(writer_client_id) >= 1) like upstream_session_id already has. Finally commands.json test.domain.expected_artifacts still lists only main.go, next_v24_sessions.sql and v24_sessions.go although client_session_fence.go and the backup_recovery.go call site are now part of the delivered increment; the dispatcher does not gate on that list, so it is a registration-completeness nit.

limitations: I reviewed the mapping and the fence as exported today. summary: The rework is real and the ten findings are genuinely gone: I rebuilt with the locked go1.27.1, got 34/34 directly and through the bound dispatcher twice (at HEAD and after cleanup), saw exit 3 NOT_IMPLEMENTED for W03-99, W03-03 and W03-02, and confirmed the archived dispatch_rework_pass.json is the same registry generation as the commands.json now on disk (its stdout/stderr hashes recompute exactly; I re-ran it myself at a34ce37a because that archived run predates the commit). AdvanceWatermark now takes the bare watermark, so 0->1, 1->3 and 3->4 all land and equal-or-backwards are refused without touching the row; all three mutators do a real expectedRevision CAS returning STALE_REVISION, sealed sessions report SESSION_SEALED on every path, and an empty writer reports MISSING_WRITER_ATTRIBUTION. The run index is globally unique over run_id and partial on NOT NULL, so a cross-project run is refused by SQLite and by the domain call, and project existence checks domain_objects kind='Project' - an id that exists as a Task is refused too. The census is now a per-table map that I falsified both synthetically (row loss, equal-total shift, removed table, empty input) and on a live database by deleting one seeded row, and the failure-atomicity test attempts version 9021 inside the poisoned transaction; committing that bump in its own transaction as a control makes the assertion flip, so it has teeth. The leaked .local/w0301-811591335 is gone and the failure path now cleans up - I proved that with a forced-failure copy of the check program that exited 1 and left no directory. P9 landed: writer attribution, lease expiry, workspace/model/build/title/archived and resume_requires_explicit_user DEFAULT 1, and the native ref is NOT NULL with minLength, which was the hard schema mismatch. P10 landed as wiring: exactly one added call in backupFence (the semantic diff is 3 lines), no-op on pre-W03 schemas, epoch regression blocked, and a barrier demanding a fresh observation before any advance, with the abort surfacing through domain.HandoffEpoch. What still stops acceptance is what the rework added on top: the three new timestamp fields are written by MapClientSession as Go's String() form rather than RFC3339 - measured, unscannable as a time, not ISO-8601, and a single column ends up with two encodings - which breaks the very WriterLease/SessionSnapshot contract P9 was chasing, and no assertion ever sets those fields; and the restore fence is unsatisfiable from production code because it demands an observation carrying the session's own writer_epoch while the only writer of runtime_observations records the run's lease_epoch (measured: the run's own lease advance succeeds on that evidence, the session's handoff stays blocked, and a synthetic epoch-3 row is the only thing that frees it), made worse by barrier rows seeded for every open session run regardless of its status or existence. Old work is intact throughout: vet clean, the three named legacy domain tests green, 0 numbered migrations touched since 6eacb1cb, all 5 receipt code hashes and all 5 registered evidence hashes recomputing, the 4 .local/data files byte-identical, 0 tracked modifications, zero of the 42 formal cases carrying any acceptance, and W03-01 still EXECUTION_REPORTED with verifier_id and accepted_at null.
